intervals.label: construction
intervals.note: The timeline dates the installation of the telescope at Mt. Hopkins to 1966-68; the Whipple page dates operation from 1968.
intervals.quote: 1966-68 Fazio and Weekes: Installation of SAO's Whipple 10m telescope at Mt. Hopkins; first purpose-built large reflector for TeV Gamma-ray Astronomy

intervals.label: operation
intervals.note: Operating span of the telescope. The gamma-ray programme was closed down in 1976-82 (separate interval); the first TeV source (the Crab Nebula) was detected in 1989 with the imaging camera installed in 1984.
intervals.quote: this telescope was in operation from 1968 until its decommissioning in 2013

intervals.label: gamma-ray programme closed down
intervals.note: The timeline says the Whipple/SAO gamma-ray programme closed down 1976-82 and that TeV gamma-ray astronomy then entered the "Dark Ages"; the gamma-ray programme was constituted again as the Whipple Collaboration in 1982.

intervals.label: telescope decommissioned
intervals.quote: this telescope was in operation from 1968 until its decommissioning in 2013

name: Whipple 10 m reflector
notes: Camera history: 37 pixels installed in 1984 (VERITAS timeline), 109 photomultipliers in the mid-1990s (arXiv:astro-ph/9602068), 379 in the final camera (Whipple page).

placements.note: Operating span from the Whipple page; the site coordinate is a site-level point.
placements.quote: The Whipple 10 m gamma-ray telescope was located at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in Southern Arizona in the United States.

energy_range.quote: The telescope operated between 300 GeV and 10 TeV.

mirror_area.quote: The Davies-Cotton reflector held 248 hexagonal mirrors and provided a total reflecting area of 75 m^2.

telescope_count.quote: The Whipple 10 m gamma-ray telescope was located at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in Southern Arizona in the United States.

summary.plain: A single 10 metre dish of 248 small mirrors that focused the faint blue flash of air showers onto a camera of photomultiplier tubes.
summary.technical: Davies-Cotton reflector, 248 hexagonal mirrors, 75 m2; camera at the focal point (37-pixel imaging camera from 1984, 109 tubes in the mid-1990s, 379 PMTs finally; 2.6 deg field of view, 0.117 deg angular resolution).

technology.quote: The Davies-Cotton reflector held 248 hexagonal mirrors and provided a total reflecting area of 75 m^2.
technology.value: Single 10 m Davies-Cotton reflector of 248 hexagonal mirrors imaging Cherenkov light onto a photomultiplier camera.
